messages:
sara: Customer AOI reporting sudden 429 spikes across regions starting ~03:20 UTC. They have Dedicated in eu-west-1 + us-east-1. Error from customer: "HTTP 429 quota_exceeded region=europe request_id=abc123". Happening on simple small-gen calls.

aj: Can you paste the full request_id + any routing headers (X-Region, X-Client-Route) and a minimal repro?

sara: request_id=abc123, X-Region: eu-west-1, X-Client-Route: default, user says ~5 qps but still 429s. Snippet from client logs:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Region: eu-west-1
Request-Id: abc123
body: {"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}
Response: 429 {"error":"quota_exhausted","region":"europe"}
```

henry: quick context: if local region reports no capacity, smart-router will failover to alternate region. If fallback happens frequently you can hit cross-region egress limits or global throttles. Look for fields route_decision and fallback_count in the routing logs.

luisa: you can check burst credits and reserved usage internally. Run:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $INT_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal-metrics/api/v1/regions/eu-west-1/credits" | jq .
```
Typical output: `{"burst_credits":0,"reserved_util":0.92,"fallback_count":7}`

support-bot: ALERT: customer=aoi exceeded burst credits in eu-west-1 at 2025-09-01T03:22:11Z (quota_status=exhausted) :warning:

aj: possible hypotheses:
- customer actually pinned to eu-west but node pool is saturated -> router falls back -> cross-region throttle -> 429.
- burst credits are fully used (luisa output) -> per-region token-level throttle.
- auth token mapping/billing flag caused early throttling if their committed usage exhausted.

maria: billing check: their committed quota shows >95% used this billing cycle. We block at threshold for Dedicated customers unless billing_override=true. Customer can sign PO or we can do a one-off top-up (requires approval).

ops-oncall: short-term mitigations:
- pin them to us-east-1 via route override (customer.route_hint = "us-east-1") if us-east capacity healthy.
- enable client retry with exponential backoff + jitter (100ms -> 2s).
- temporary top-up of burst credits for eu-west-1 while billing gets sorted.

henry: also consider cold-start/warmup: model kernel selection + KV-cache miss can create short bursts that burn credits. Recommend a warmup script: send 5 warmup requests per GPU at low priority before traffic shift.

aj: repro steps I recommend to confirm behavior locally:
1) set header `X-Region: eu-west-1`
2) run 50 concurrent requests (seq len 256) for 60s
3) tail router logs: grep request_id route_decision fallback_count
Expected: if region is saturated you will see fallback_count > 0 then some responses 429 from fallback due to egress throttle.

sara: ran the repro in staging and saw fallback_count=4 and a mix of 200/429. Forwarding logs to infra. Customer approved escalation for immediate top-up.

aj: ok. @luisa can you validate burst credit top-up and whether a temporary billing_override is needed? I can open an infra ticket with the routing logs attached.

luisa: checking now, will post internal txn id when done. If we top-up, monitor reserved_util for 10m then remove top-up (to avoid sticky billing). :eyes:

maria: i'll prepare the invoicing note. We need PO to make it permanent. If customer confirms, we can approve one-time credit.

ops-oncall: next actions checklist: pin-route (if approved), top-up burst (infra), enable client-retry guidance (support doc), follow up billing PO. Who's owning?

sara: I will own coordination with customer. aj please escalate infra ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
